newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Lumber rejects California assets for forest.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Lumber rejects California assets for forest.

text.p: The Pacific Lumber Co. said on Tuesday it rejected a wide-ranging list of properties offered by the state of California in exchange for ancient redwood groves.
The decision was a setback to government efforts to acquire and preserve northern California's Headwaters grove, the world's largest privately-owned old-growth redwood forest.
Pacific Lumber said it did not find any of the properties offered by the state "acceptable for exchange," and asked state officials to offer cash instead.

The U.S. and California governments reached a tentative agreement last Sept. 28 with Pacific Lumber and its parent company, MAXXAM Inc., to preserve about 7,500 acres of virgin old growth forests and buffers, including Headwaters and Elk Head Springs forest.
The groves, about 250 miles (400 kms) north of San Francisco, contain towering redwoods, some of which are hundreds or even thousands of years old.
The parties agreed that they would identify $380 million in government assets to be swapped for the forests -- $250 million of them from the federal government and $130 million from the state.

California gave MAXXAM a choice of surplus properties estimated to be worth more than $200 million. Its offerings included office buildings, warehouses, a rock quarry and a bus terminal in San Francisco.
In a statement, Pacific Lumber said it gave the state's properties "full and careful consideration" but concluded the assets were not acceptable.
Pacific Lumber President John Campbell said some of the properties would have been difficult to transfer and others were withdrawn from the list by the state.
"Also, at public meetings in several California cities, citizens expressed opposition to swapping forest lands or other real estate in their respective areas for Headwaters," he said.

Pacific Lumber said it would continue to work with the state to fulfill the Headwaters agreement, but added that the state should "proceed with the steps necessary to assure it can provide cash" for its portion of the agreement.

The company said it was still talking to the federal government about its part of the compensation package. The U.S. government has offered MAXXAM other timber land, oil and gas interests and land in exchange for the redwood groves.
California Secretary for Resources Doug Wheeler said Pacific Lumber's decision was "regrettable" but would not stop the state's efforts to acquire Headwaters Forest.
